report.summary:
Step 1 is done. All the wave-1 imaging work now runs in the live scene, in both labs and in the capture harness. The final capture set (i1final) scores 154 of 228 on the matched pipeline and 157 of 228 lossless. The baseline was 133 of 229 and 137 of 229. The current tree before my changes scored 128 of 229 (set i1pre).

Every family that passed in the baseline still passes as many rows, except Noise: 15 against 16. The two noise rows that differ (grey 200-219, and grey 220-239, which now has no samples) were already lost on the pre-integration capture of the same tree. They follow S2's profile refit, made after the baseline was taken, so my changes did not cause them. One integration bug did regress noise: in the first integrated set (i1a) temporal noise SD rose to 3.64. The dose-rate controller gives 12% fewer counts at the 200 mm field than the S2 noise fit assumed. I fixed that with a 230/200 rescale, and noise SD is now 3.38.

What now works:
- **Heart motion (S3):** driven by one CardiacClock per lab. The aortic root, the ostia and the legacy catheter path move together, and coronaries use the dense render path. All six landmark-speed rows now pass: LCA 2.7-3.9 rose to 16-21.5 mm/s, RCA 4.2/13.3 rose to 24.3/47.2 mm/s. All four catheter-motion rows pass: shaft range 3.3 rose to 15.2 px.
- **Thorax (S4):** per-patient thorax with the beating heart silhouette merged in, ThoraxSegmentPass fed, lung clutter uniforms set, and ECG electrodes and table drawn by default.
- **Dose-rate control (S6):** the controller replaces the old kV formula. Each lab keeps a controller and a DoseTracker, exposed through `labImaging.pci` / `labImaging.diagnostic` for a dose panel later. The renderer's meter reading feeds the closed loop as the rendered patient's path. Without that the PCI lab under-exposed by 17%.
- **Image chain (S2):** mode, framesSinceStart and profile are passed. Both labs size the canvas in device pixels with `fitCanvas` (verified in the PCI lab: 1280 px canvas, render 1024, no fallback, no GL error).
- **Capture harness (S0):** installed from main.tsx in dev builds; `npm run realism` added.

Measured decisions:
- **Segment integrator (S2b) stays off by default.** With it on: 146 against 150, vessel and catheter rows the same within 0.1 px, about 8 ms more per frame in capture mode, and the capture harness misses the moved catheter and iodine.
- **Controller gains stay "legacy-ap".** Physical gains scored 145 against 150.
- ECG and table on (150 against 149 without) and the thorax segment pass on (150 against 149 with the ribbon thorax).

Performance: scene build is 1.4-4.2 ms of CPU per frame. A pipelined frame takes 4.8 ms at 768 px and 8.3 ms at 1024 px, far inside the 66.7 ms that 15 frames/s needs. In capture mode it is 3.5-4.5 ms for the scene plus 17-21 ms for render and read-back.

**Things I could not fix from my files:**
- I patched `XrayRenderer.prototype.render` from sceneBuilder.ts so every renderer registers the thorax pass and sets the clutter uniforms. It reads the renderer's private `pAnat` program, and S2 should move this into `XrayRenderer.ts`.
- The trabecular bone texture is not integrated, because it needs a change to the renderer's bone shader.

**Problems in other tracks' areas, seen when I compared frames with real runs:**
- **Contrast:** washes out completely by mid-run. This is the contrast-transport work of my next steps.
- **Motion (S3):** too large in RAO views; the SA nodal artery shows as a beaded chain of dots.
- **Anatomy (S4):** faint heart silhouette; a uniform spine band with box-like vertebrae; the radial guide enters RAO views from the side instead of from the top.
- **Vessels (S2b/S2):** large vessels are too wide and flat-topped.

Details and exact suggested changes for the owners of those files are in docs/realism/wave2/I1.md.

report.summary:
The step 2 review items are fixed, re-verified and documented. The headline score improved even with the fake syringe tail removed: the matched pipeline went from 168 of 233 to 171 of 235, lossless from 171 of 233 to 174 of 235, and Timing is now 56 of 66 (60 of 66 lossless). One target got worse: the end-of-run contrast level is now 0.15 of the peak against the real 0.44.

High (contrast slowing beyond chronic stenoses, contrastTransport.ts): the transport had read S9's whole rest-reserve share as collateral, so an 85% LAD behaved like a TIMI 1 vessel. Chronic non-occlusive lesions now use a + (1 - a) x CHRONIC_RESERVE_ANTEGRADE (0.57), where a is S9's raw antegrade share. Acute thrombotic lesions and occlusions keep the raw share. I set 0.57 so the frame count beyond an 80-90% stenosis averages 1.31 times normal on three library cases, matching Li et al. 2021 (corrected TIMI frame count 28.56 vs 21.64, a ratio of 1.32; abstract opened through PubMed, doi 10.3389/fcvm.2021.718935). Per severity: 80% 1.12-1.16, 85% 1.24-1.40, 90% 1.32-1.55. The distal LAD now reaches 0.83-0.86 strength inside the 3.4 s run (0.87-0.89 without a lesion; the review measured 0.16 at 85%).

Missing scope (live flows): transportNet now takes live flow conditions. An inflated balloon stops contrast beyond it, hyperaemia speeds the tree up, and slow flow is regional, beyond the treated lesion. The scene builder takes these through a new flowMods field, and the PCI lab sets them with a new pciFlowMods function. Slow flow is no longer a whole-side flowScale of 0.3.

Medium (syringe tail, injection.ts): the 0.9 s release is withdrawn. Release is now 0.1 s, a labelled model parameter, and syringe and line compliance are neglected, as the code and facts file now say. Flow falls below 5% of the plateau within 0.3 s of the push, and the release delivers 0.1-0.3 mL. The standard push was recalibrated against the library: 1.8, 2.2 and 2.5 s pushes scored 48, 56 and 56 of 66 timing rows, and I chose 2.2 s because it uses less contrast. A standard run is now 8.5 mL left and 5.3 mL right through a 6 Fr guide. Traces and the Injector record the push and release volumes separately, and the PCI panel shows both. Any persistence after the push now comes only from the transport.

Low items:
- **Hand limit:** now a plunger force: 50 psi on the 10 mL control syringe's barrel, 56.9 N. Zhang's abstract does not give the syringe size, so this is a labelled assumption. A narrower barrel reaches a higher pressure (8.7 mm: 131 psi). A 5 Fr diagnostic catheter still reaches only 1.4 mL/s. A new test shows it opacifies more dilutely than 6 Fr (proximal LAD 0.90, mid 0.61, against 0.97 and 0.87). The diagnostic lab keeps 6 Fr as a stated model choice.
- **Catheter lumen:** it now fills from the hub as the dead volume is pushed. It follows only the guide's own injection, so a contralateral run no longer fills the guide. The PCI lab has a new 'Flush guide' button that leaves saline in the lumen.
- **Scorecard:** rewritten with report.py's denominators throughout. It now says plainly which targets are slower or lower than the real runs.

Volume accounting: the PCI debrief now uses the volume the syringes actually pushed. In the browser, a standard run plus a puff gave 11 mL. In the diagnostic lab, Shift+click on the inject buttons gives a test puff. Hold from those buttons is not possible, because they fire on click, after the pointer is up.

defects.issue: Contrast slows far too much beyond chronic stenoses of 80-95%, and this breaks the main PCI teaching case. transportNet (lines 153-158) multiplies each region's resting flow by min(1, hypFactor*(1-collateral)*cfr). For chronic lesions, S9's 'collateral' share also includes the MP_CHRONIC_REST_RESERVE term, so the antegrade share is close to zero: 0.045 at 90% and 0.003 at 95%. Distal samples then fall back to the 20 mm/s MIN_SPEED_MM_S floor, which is a numerical floor, not physics. Measured with vite-node on CASE_LIBRARY[0] anatomy: LAD theta at 90% of the vessel length is 1.60 s with no lesion, 1.57 s at 70%, 2.58 s at 80%, 5.62 s at 85%, 6.58 s at 90% and 6.79 s at 95%. With the PCI lab's first scenario lesion (LAD 85%, position 0.38, 12 mm) and a standard injection, the point 85% along the LAD peaks at 0.16 strength within the 3.4 s run, against 0.88 without the lesion. A stable 85% LAD therefore shows TIMI 1-like flow and the distal vessel never opacifies. The stenosis test checks only 50% against 95%, so it does not catch this.
defects.fix: Base the slowing on antegrade resting flow, not on S9's reserve-inflated collateral share. Options: use demand*min(1, S9 antegrade*cfr) for the antegrade part and treat the reserve term as antegrade, or cap the slowing so that non-occlusive chronic stenoses keep TIMI 3 with a moderately raised frame count. Calibrate against published corrected TIMI frame counts for stenoses if a source can be opened, otherwise label it as a model parameter. Add tests at 80, 85 and 90% asserting that the distal vessel fills inside a standard run, and at 99% or CTO asserting delayed or collateral filling.

defects.issue: HAND_FALL_S = 0.9 s was tuned to hit the end-of-run level and washout targets, but it does this by keeping the injection going rather than through transport washout. In the standard left plan, flow is still 2.03 mL/s 0.5 s after the push ends, 1.07 mL/s at 3.0 s and 0.45 mL/s at the 3.4 s run end, and the total is 9.1 mL instead of about 7.2 mL. The facts file attributes the tail to 'the pressurised syringe and line discharge', but the model has no compliance term. The 'distal persistence' the step asks for, and the 0.44 of peak at run end, therefore come mostly from contrast still flowing in, and the PCI cine (pushEnd + CINE_TAIL_S) ends while the syringe is still delivering.
defects.fix: Model the release as fast, or add an explicit syringe and tubing compliance with a sourced or measured value. Get the end-of-run persistence from the transport instead (laminar share, wall retention, distal persistence), then recalibrate against the harness. Report the plateau volume and the tail volume separately in the panel.

defects.issue: The Catheter family dropped from 4 to 1 of 4: the 'unfilled guide' lumen contrast is 0 against a real band of 3.0-25.4, and wall separation is 1.75 px against 4.0-6.0. The proposed remedy is for S0 to measure the fluoroscopy companion, whose lumen holds saline. The PCI lab never shows that state, though: the guide Injector starts with primed: 1 and the scene is given catheterContrast = guide.primed during fluoroscopy, so the guide always looks contrast-filled in the lab. The harness change would hide the difference rather than test what users see. In addition, lumenShare = injecting ? 1 : ... (line 507) draws the main catheter full of contrast during a contralateral (CTO) injection, because `injecting` belongs to the contra trace. It also draws the lumen full of contrast while a flushed lumen is still pushing out its saline dead volume.
defects.fix: Decide, with evidence, what the lumen holds between runs (for example dilution after the manifold returns to pressure, or flush events), and render the lab's actual state in the capture harness. Tie lumenShare to the guide's own injector or trace, not to whichever bolus is active. Let the lumen fill progressively as the dead volume clears.

defects.issue: MAX_HAND_PRESSURE_PSI = 50 combined with 37 deg C viscosity limits a 5 Fr diagnostic catheter to 1.4 mL/s, below the model's left resting coronary flow of 2.3 mL/s. Every diagnostic-lab injection through 6 Fr sits at the hand limit (2.8 mL/s, 47 psi). Routine 5 Fr diagnostic angiography by hand opacifies well, so the cap or its application to a 10 mL control syringe looks wrong. The implementer worked around it by switching the diagnostic lab to 6 Fr instead of questioning it.
defects.fix: Check which syringe size and catheter the Zhang 2016 limit applies to. Small control syringes reach higher pressures, so make the cap depend on syringe bore, or record the limitation as a model parameter with a test that 5 Fr diagnostic catheters can still reach adequate opacification.

defects.issue: The totals use inconsistent denominators. The summary gives i1s2final as '168 of 233' and step 1 as '154 of 228', while the family table's TOTAL row gives 168/235 and 154/234. The headline also calls fill 10-90% 'matched' when the median is 1.53 s against 1.33/1.27 s (15-20% slow), peak time is 2.57 s against 2.13 s, and LCA AP-CRA rise fails at 1.93 s against a band of 0.48-1.49.

report.summary:
Track I2 review fixes are done. All the high and medium review items are handled. Typecheck is clean and the full suite passes (911 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed). Four results still miss their real targets, as listed in the open issues: crossings, the LM+LAD length, LAD across-vessel motion and the LAD 20-60 mm band.

1. **LAD depth (high).** The height clamp had no working floor. It now uses the smaller of hMin and the height before the undulation, for every vessel. The LAD mid course is lifted 2 mm into the groove fat, and its height stays smoothly between 0.6 and 8 mm above the myocardium. A bridged run keeps its depth.
   - On 124 trees, LAD samples below -1 mm outside a bridge went from 2,602 (in 113 trees, deepest -15.8 mm) to 0. The minimum height is now +0.6 mm.
   - The fix also found a bridge (CASE_LIBRARY large-root-0) that had floated out of the myocardium and lost its flag. All 7 genome bridges are now flagged.
   - The honest 20-60 mm band is 12.7° (real 13.85°). The review settings gave 10.6° once the floor applied.
2. **Named-branch truncation (high).** The PDA now has course variants. Two new rules: a branch may run beside its parent or a sibling for a few mm near its origin, and a crowded PL3 or late septal is left out instead of drawn as a stub. Diagonals, marginals and posterolateral branches now try origins a few mm along the parent; narrower diagonals reach further; the ramus can turn towards the LAD.

defects.issue: deriveMaster only counts final-assessment exam passes with `e.date > from`, where `from` is the level IV award date. A component exam passed on the same day level IV was awarded is ignored. Challenge.tsx turns on the final-assessment Start button (`ready = awarded >= 4`) as soon as level IV is awarded, so a learner who goes straight on loses a held-out rung-5+ case and gets no credit. Probe (scratchpad vitest on deriveMaster): all five components passed at rung 5 on the L4 award day gives passed=false; the same rows dated the next day give passed=true.
defects.fix: Compare by timestamp, not date. Record the `t` of the exam that completed level IV and accept component passes with a later t. If day granularity is kept, disable Start in Challenge.tsx until the day after the award and say why.

defects.issue: Each diagnostic exam pool is fixed and small. Measured: 3 cases per rung, so 18 per EPA, 12 at rung 3 or above and only 6 at rung 5 or above. pickExamCase toward level III draws from every rung of 3 or above, so it often uses up rung-5/6 cases. Every failure, abandoned attempt or critical-error reset at level IV uses another one, and the final assessment needs at least one more unseen rung-5+ case per component. With about 2 failures the pool runs out and schedule.ts returns 'The exam pool is exhausted for this level' with no way forward. The learner is then locked out of levels IV and V for that EPA, and so out of the final assessment, permanently.
defects.fix: Have the level III exam draw only from rungs 3-4. Generate held-out cases on demand from fresh X-prefixed seeds, which the seeded generator supports without limit, filtered to the rung's key range, instead of a fixed 3 per rung. Or at least make the pool much larger and keep some cases back for the final assessment. Add a test that runs fail, fail, critical error, pass and so on through to level V without running out.

defects.issue: Reading exams can be retaken without limit. setNo = Date.now(), so every set gets a new id (angio-exam:<drill>:<setNo>), and isExamCase accepts any setNo. The rule that only the first attempt counts therefore never applies to reading. Sets are drawn again and again from the same held-out pool: for example the occlusion drill has only 18 distinct runs across 10 sets, and a second set shares 4 of its 6 items with the first. Abandoning a set logs nothing, and failed sets never reset progress because reading exams have no critical errors. diag-report, a final-assessment component, can reach level IV this way just by retrying.
defects.fix: Track the held-out runs each learner has seen and build exam sets only from unseen runs, or limit exam sets to one per drill per day toward each level. Log an abandoned set as a failed exam. Give the level III/IV award for reading a rule that resets on failure, or count failures against it.
